usages.explain: Placed at the beginning of a sentence, used to draw a conclusion based on newly acquired information. 「じゃ」 is often extended to "じゃあ" and is a familiar way of saying "では".

examples.content: 彼は日本に4年住んでいるんですよ。では、日本語が上手ですね。
examples.transcription: かれ、にっぽんに4ねんすんでいるんですよ。じゃ、にほんごがじょうずですね。
examples.mean: He has lived in Japan for four years. So, your Japanese is good.

examples.content: 急用があっちゃって。じゃ、映画を見に行けないの。
examples.transcription: きゅうようがあっちゃって。じゃ、えいがをみにいけないの。
examples.mean: I had something urgent to do. So I can't go see a movie.

title: じゃ(あ) / では => If so, Well (then), In that case
